data.title: S&P 500 reports weekly losses as technology rout weighs on markets
data.description:
Wall Street's major averages ended mixed on Friday, with the Nasdaq leading a recovery from its worst day in more than a year.

The benchmark S&P 500 (SP500) gained 0.3%, while the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite finished advanced 1.1%, while the blue-chip Dow ended down 0.5%.

However, the S&P 500 also slipped 2.68% for the week.

From a sector-level perspective, six S&P 500 sectors ended the week in positive territory, while five finished in the red.

Seeking Alpha analyst Jack Bowman highlighted that this week was a wild week for stocks, and after the flush on Thursday, he is surprised that there are still gains to be had this week among sectors. 

Communication Services (XLC) and Consumer Discretionary (XLY) were the strongest performing sectors this week, with gains of 4.93% and 1.97%, respectively.

The analyst added that Communications and Consumer Discretionary were up despite the attribution from big tech firms like Alphabet, Meta, and Amazon. This showed a broadening of breadth on the week, which is a positive sign for our bull market, although it was not enough to save the index by a long shot. Big tech is just too concentrated.

Conversely, Energy (XLE) and Technology (XLK) posted the weakest weekly performances, falling 11.52% and 8.19%, respectively.

Bowman argued that we can see that the losers in the index were concentrated in technology and energy. Energy is responding to oil, which fell following the election on hopes of peace in the Middle East, although that is highly speculative.

“The big flush happened in tech as AI fears permeated the market. I am still bullish on big tech, as its valuations are now making it one of the cheapest in the market. And that's a considerable positive for tech investors that have wanted to load up but were cautious of valuations more broadly. I wouldn't be too concerned about the energy drop, as it has run up significantly and was overbought, so this could be a correction that preserves long-term momentum,” Bowman concluded.

Weekly S&P 500 sector performance:

  • Communication Services Select Sector SPDR Fund (XLC): +4.93%
  • Consumer Discretionary Select Sector SPDR Fund (XLY): +1.97%
  • Real Estate Select Sector SPDR Fund (XLRE): +1.95%
  • Financials Select Sector SPDR Fund (XLF): +1.20%
  • Consumer Staples Select Sector SPDR Fund (XLP): +0.76%
  • Health Care Select Sector SPDR Fund (XLV): +0.16%
  • Utilities Select Sector SPDR Fund (XLU): -0.69%
  • Materials Select Sector SPDR Fund (XLB): -1.46%
  • Industrials Select Sector SPDR Fund (XLI): -2.8%
  • Technology Select Sector SPDR Fund (XLK): -8.19%
  • Energy Select Sector SPDR Fund (XLE): -11.95%

data.title: U.S. indexes will hit new highs within three months, says SA analyst
data.description:
Seeking Alpha analyst Alex King of Cestrian Capital Research expects the major Wall Street indexes to hit new highs within the next three months.

“On Thursday this week, the AI trade nearly died but was immediately resuscitated by a never-ending slew of social media posts from politicians, financiers, and vendors about how everyone was still very committed to (i) AI and (ii) each other,” he said.

U.S. stocks pushed to recover from the ongoing technology selloff. The benchmark S&P 500 (SP500) ended +0.3%, while the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite (COMP:IND) finished +1.1%, and the blue-chip Dow (DJI) closed -0.5%.

In addition, the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index (SOX) jumped 4.2%, while the Nasdaq 100 (QQQ) turned around and ended 1.5%.

Top semiconductors on Friday included Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing (TSM) +6.2%, Broadcom (AVGO) +0.6%, Micron Technology (MU) +5.2%, and Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) +10.6%.

“Frankenstein’s monster lives, and we believe it will march right back up the hill,” King said. “We anticipate new all-time highs in the equity indices within three months.”

data.title: SiriusPoint expects LPT to free over $200M and lift BSCR by around 20 points
data.description:
Earnings Call Insights: SiriusPoint (SPNT) Q3 2026

Management view

  • "Before I turn to the results, I want to welcome John Sauerland to our Board of Directors" (CEO & Director Scott Egan).

  • "The third quarter saw SiriusPoint deliver another strong performance with attractive underwriting margins, disciplined growth and returns above our 12% to 15% ROE target range" (CEO & Director Egan).

  • "The third quarter saw us deliver 20% growth in Insurance & Services and a Core Combined ratio of 90.1%" and "Our operating return on equity was 17.6%" (CEO & Director Egan).

  • "Today’s announcement [is] that we have entered into a loss portfolio transfer agreement with RiverStone that will substantially cover our remaining runoff exposures" and "following completion, our runoff exposures will be at de minimis levels" (CEO & Director Egan).

  • "[The LPT] frees up capital tied to these legacy reserves of over $200 million on completion and will increase our BSCR ratio by around 20 points" and "we will continue with our current buyback program" (CEO & Director Egan).

  • "Core gross written premium increased 14% to $991 million" and "Operating earnings per diluted share were $0.88" (CFO & Principal Accounting Officer James McKinney).

Outlook

  • "The transaction is subject to customary regulatory approvals" and "in an ideal world... we would get it done in Q4" and "Could it slip into Q1? Maybe" (CEO & Director Egan).

  • "We expect A&H premiums to return to low single-digit growth in the fourth quarter, while the pipeline entering 2027 remains encouraging" (CFO McKinney).

  • "Looking specifically to the fourth quarter, the nonrenewal of a FinPro program... is expected to result in Specialty P&C premiums being modestly lower year-over-year" and "We expect growth to resume in 2027" (CFO McKinney).

  • "The expected day 1 cost of the LPT is approximately $60 million" and "on a go-forward basis, we expect runoff losses to have a negligible impact" (CFO McKinney).

Financial results

  • "The core combined ratio was 90.1%, resulting in underwriting income of $76 million" and "Total investment income was $69 million, including $66 million of net investment income" (CFO McKinney).

  • "Net services fee income increased 21% year-over-year to $12 million" and "Operating net income was $103 million for the third quarter" (CFO McKinney).

  • "Diluted book value per share, excluding AOCI, increased by $0.73 during the quarter to $20.21" (CFO McKinney).

  • "Our estimated BSCR ratio was 232%" and "Following $27 million of common share repurchases in the quarter, $74 million remains under our authorization" (CFO McKinney).

Q&A

  • Michael Phillips, Oppenheimer: "Can you talk about [international A&H] a bit? Why was it exited...?" CEO & Director Egan: "For us, this was a performance reason. We weren't getting the traction that we wanted on the underwriting actions" and "it's not really a huge deal."

  • Michael Phillips, Oppenheimer: "I'm just looking... it's around $15 million, $16 million a year. Is that the right number to see?" CFO McKinney: "Yes... that's relatively the right number to consider." Phillips: "how long does this -- its business written before 2023?" CFO McKinney: "it basically has about a 3-year -- 2.5- to 3-year tail."

  • Michael Phillips, Oppenheimer: "does this recast say anything about the strategic rationale... the way you view reinsurance...?" CEO & Director Egan: "No, definitely not" and "I would not read that reinsurance in any way is not strategically important to the business."

  • Rowland Mayor, RBC Capital Markets: "Is there any further balance sheet optimization going forward?" CEO & Director Egan: "There's definitely a little bit more work that we probably do in the debt stack" and "99% of our efforts are in the go-forward potential of the business." CFO McKinney: "we... anticipate... less than kind of $100 million... deployed" in minority MGA elements and "we'll be able to... further optimize the debt stack of the company."

  • Rowland Mayor, RBC Capital Markets: "was the $27 million in the quarter impacted by the LPT?" and "Do you still expect to complete the authorization this year?" CFO McKinney: "The answer to both of those questions is yes" and "we intend to... restart the program."

  • Rowland Mayor, RBC Capital Markets: "I didn't see an expected close on the LPT." CEO & Director Egan: "We never try and forecast regulatory approval" and "in an ideal world... [Q4]... Could it slip into Q1? Maybe."

  • Andrew Andersen, Jefferies: "which businesses are contributing most to [the '27] pipeline...?" CEO & Director Egan: "I would probably highlight our MGA Global Programs business, as having a very strong and healthy pipeline" and "our A&H business, we're feeling quite upbeat going into 2027." CFO McKinney: "the mix shift... led to... the difference... between... gross written premium growth" and "as we go into 2027, there's an opportunity... you'll see more of our gross premium written... into the net written premium."

  • Andrew Andersen, Jefferies: "on employer stop loss... rate around 20%..." CEO & Director Egan: "Within U.S. Medical excess of loss, we are seeing rate expectations in excess of 20%" and "we are broadly carrying rate in line with claims inflation."

  • Timothy D'Agostino, B. Riley Securities: "Do you... potentially redomiciling...?" CEO & Director Egan: "in terms of our legal entity structure, that's something that we'll continue to evaluate" and "we're happy with the structure as it stands at the moment." CFO McKinney: "I would not overly focus on whether that is U.S. or Bermuda or another... the key element is what is the mix of the business going on."

  • Charles Peters, Raymond James: "Can you speak to... what lines of business you're getting favorable development from?" CEO & Director Egan: "we actually reserve above our price loss ratio" and "nothing is going to change in terms of our reserving approach." CFO McKinney: "we're seeing it favorable development across the portfolio."

Sentiment analysis

  • Analysts: slightly negative, with detailed probing on exits, LPT mechanics, capital actions, and structural questions such as domicile (e.g., "Do you -- like is there benefits to potentially redomiciling?").

  • Management: slightly positive and confident in prepared remarks and largely steady in Q&A, emphasizing volatility reduction and closure of legacy exposure (e.g., "Put simply, this transaction allows us to effectively close the chapter on the legacy book once and for all" (CEO & Director Egan)).

  • Versus last quarter: management tone stayed confident on discipline and cycle management, while analyst focus shifted from competition and product initiatives to the LPT’s practical impacts (timing, admin costs, repurchase resumption) and reporting/structure changes.

Quarter-over-quarter comparison

  • "Core Combined ratio" moved from "91.4%" in Q2 to "90.1%" in Q3 (CEO & Director Egan).

  • Operating return on equity increased from "13.8%" in Q2 to "17.6%" in Q3 (CEO & Director Egan).

  • Capital strength messaging shifted from "Our estimated BSCR ratio remains strong at 239%" in Q2 to "Our estimated BSCR ratio was 232%" in Q3 alongside a pro forma uplift expectation tied to the LPT (CFO McKinney).

  • Strategic emphasis broadened in Q3 to include "a loss portfolio transfer agreement with RiverStone" and a reporting change where "Accident & Health... becomes a stand-alone segment" beginning in Q4 (CEO & Director Egan).

Risks and concerns

  • "Pricing becomes more competitive in multiple lines of business" (CEO & Director Egan).

  • "Financial and professional lines remain competitive, particularly in D&O and professional liability" and "in Property Catastrophe Reinsurance... we expect continued pricing pressure" (CFO McKinney).

  • "Across both segments, losses recognized to date in relation to the Middle East conflict remain limited" (CFO McKinney).

Final takeaway

SiriusPoint’s management presented Q3 as another quarter of core underwriting and investment-driven returns above its 12% to 15% across-the-cycle ROE target, while highlighting a RiverStone loss portfolio transfer intended to reduce runoff volatility, move legacy exposures to “de minimis levels,” and (upon closing) free over $200 million of capital with an estimated BSCR benefit of around 20 points; management also outlined a forthcoming segment reporting change that will break out Accident & Health as a stand-alone segment beginning in Q4, alongside plans to resume share repurchases after the LPT announcement.

data.title: Nasdaq achieves a 1% advance; indexes see big losses for the week
data.description:
Wall Street's major averages ended mixed on Friday, with the Nasdaq leading a recovery from its worst day in more than a year.

The benchmark S&P 500 (SP500) closed +0.3%, while the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite (COMP:IND) finished +1.1%, and the blue-chip Dow (DJI) ended -0.5%.

Week-to-date, the indexes were down. The S&P 500 was down 2.7%, while the Nasdaq lost 3.4%, and the Dow declined 0.9%.

Among the top decliners on Friday were Axon Enterprise (AXON) -17.9%, Microchip Technology (MCHP) -10.2%, and Insulet Corp. (PODD) -6.2%.

“On Thursday this week, the AI trade nearly died but was immediately resuscitated by a never-ending slew of social media posts from politicians, financiers, and vendors about how everyone was still very committed to (i) AI and (ii) each other,” said Seeking Alpha analyst Alex King of Cestrian Capital Research.

“And lo and behold, on Friday the Philadelphia SOX duly jumped 4.2%, the Nasdaq-100 1.5%, and the S&P500 0.3%. Frankenstein’s monster lives, and we believe it will march right back up the hill. We anticipate new all-time highs in the equity indices within three months,” King added.

On the economic front, nonfarm payrolls surged in October, sending the unemployment rate lower.

Over to the bond market, yields rose after the jobs report. The 10-year Treasury yield (US10Y) rose 3 basis points to 4.87%, while the 2-year Treasury yield (US2Y) also rose 6 basis points to 4.53%. The 30-year Treasury yield (US30Y) was 1 basis point higher at 5.27%.

Oil prices were mostly unchanged. Crude oil futures (CL1:COM) were $90, while Brent (CO1:COM) was $98 per barrel.

The U.S. dollar (DXY) rose 0.7%.

data.title: JD.com shares rose for seven consecutive sessions
data.description:
JD.com (JD) shares rose for seven straight sessions as the stock was up 1.8% at $29.15 on Friday.

The supply chain-based technology and service provider gained nearly 12% in the preceding six sessions. JD is up 10% over the past one month, while the stock has risen 1.3% so far this year, compared to a 7% rise in the broader S&P 500 Index (SP500).

"Advertising and commission revenues are growing faster than product sales, boosting JD Retail’s gross margin for the 17th consecutive quarter. JD’s robust net cash position funds buybacks, while management guides for accelerating profit growth and long-term high single-digit retail margins," pointed out a recent Seeking Alpha analysis.

Looking at Seeking Alpha's Quant Rating, JD has a Hold rating with a score of 3.3 out of 5. The company received an A in the prospect of growth, while it got a C in momentum factor.

Turning to the Wall Street community, 31 analysts gave JD a Buy and above rating. Three analysts have given the stock a Hold recommendation, while none recommended Strong Sell.

Seeking Alpha analysts are positive and see the stock as a Buy.

data.title: DraftKings shares fall sharply, ending six-session winning streak
data.description:
DraftKings (NASDAQ: DKNG) snapped its six-session winning streak on Friday, with shares closing 21.28% lower at $18.52.

Despite Friday's decline, the stock had gained 15.85% over the preceding six sessions, compared with a 5.04% decline in the S&P 500 Index. Year-to-date, DKNG has fallen 50.38%, while the broader index has gained 7.43%.

The selloff followed the company's Q3 results, with revenue rising 16% year-over-year to $1.33B but missing the $1.39B analyst consensus. Non-GAAP EPS came in at -$0.53, missing expectations by $0.28, while adjusted EBITDA recorded a loss of $316.9M against the expected loss of $65.9M.

Despite the earnings miss, monthly unique paying customers increased 13% year-over-year to 4.1M. Sports revenue grew 31.5% to $783.6M, while iGaming revenue rose 2.1% to $460.9M.

Looking ahead, DraftKings lowered its FY2026 revenue  outlook to $6.35B-$6.55B, below the $6.65B analyst consensus, with adjusted EBITDA of $175M-$275M. For FY2027, it projects revenue of $7.35B-$7.75B and adjusted EBITDA of $800M-$1B, while planning to invest $650M-$700M in its Predictions business in FY2026.

Despite the recent weakness, Seeking Alpha analyst Caffital Research maintained a bullish view on DraftKings in September, citing its stable sports-betting market share and rapid growth in its Predictions business. The analyst estimated 54% upside, with a price target of $32.60.

According to Seeking Alpha's Quant ratings, DraftKings carries a Hold rating with a score of 3.05 out of 5, receiving an A+ for growth, C- for profitability, and D- for valuation.

Wall Street sentiment remained strongly bullish, with the average analyst rating at Strong Buy (4.50/5). Of the 36 analysts covering the stock, 30 rated it Buy or Strong Buy, five assigned a Hold rating, and one gave it a Sell rating.

Seeking Alpha analysts remained cautious, maintaining a Hold rating with an average score of 3.40 out of 5.

data.title: Trupanion expects $179M-$182M of adjusted operating income in 2026 while advancing a new digital product launch next summer
data.description:
Earnings Call Insights: Trupanion (TRUP) Q3 2026

Management View

  • "I'm pleased to report that our third quarter results were strong, led by adjusted operating income in excess of $47 million, an all-time high." (President, CEO & Director Margaret Tooth)

  • "We added over 20,500 net new pets, an increase in excess of 28% over Q3 of last year, and our acquisition spend per pet declined modestly, driven largely by improved conversion." (President, CEO & Director Tooth)

  • "Retention improved for the seventh consecutive quarter" and "claims automation has climbed from under 15% in 2020 to over 65% today." (President, CEO & Director Tooth)

  • "We remain on track to launch by the midpoint of our strategic plan next summer." (President, CEO & Director Tooth)

  • "We've begun limited trials" for Landspath and "move closer to launch in 2027." (President, CEO & Director Tooth)

  • "In October, we announced a new partnership with television personality and music executive, Simon Cowell." (President, CEO & Director Tooth)

  • "Total revenue for the quarter was $405.6 million, up 11% year-over-year." (Chief Financial Officer Fawwad Qureshi)

  • "In Q3, we repurchased approximately 830,000 shares at a cost of approximately $25 million." (Chief Financial Officer Qureshi)

Outlook

  • "For the full year of 2026, we now expect total revenue in the range of $1.59 billion to $1.597 billion" and "total adjusted operating income to be between $179 million and $182 million." (Chief Financial Officer Qureshi)

  • "For the fourth quarter of 2026, total revenue is expected to be in the range of $407 million to $414 million" and "total adjusted operating income is expected to be in the range of $48 million to $51 million." (Chief Financial Officer Qureshi)

  • "The existing book of business beginning to move to a new underwriting partner in the fourth quarter of 2026" as the company proceeds with ending the Pets Best relationship after Q3 2028. (Chief Financial Officer Qureshi)

  • "For our fourth quarter and full year guidance, we used a 72% conversion rate in our projections." (Chief Financial Officer Qureshi)

Financial Results

  • "Within our Subscription Business, revenue was $287.9 million" and "Other Business revenue was $117.7 million for the quarter." (Chief Financial Officer Qureshi)

  • "Total monthly average revenue per pet for the quarter was $88.95" and "Total subscription pets increased 6% year-over-year to 1,145,000 pets as of September 30." (Chief Financial Officer Qureshi)

  • "Average monthly retention for the trailing 12 months was 98.38%" and "The quarter included adverse prior period development of $0.6 million." (Chief Financial Officer Qureshi)

  • "In total, adjusted operating income was $47 million in Q3" and "net income for the quarter was $9.3 million or $0.21 per basic and diluted share." (Chief Financial Officer Qureshi)

  • "Our free cash flow was $28.5 million, an all-time high" and "Over the last 4 quarters, free cash flow reached $86.7 million." (Chief Financial Officer Qureshi)

  • "We ended the quarter with $396.8 million in cash and short-term investments" and "Subsequent to quarter end, we repaid $15 million of outstanding borrowings." (Chief Financial Officer Qureshi)

Q&A

  • Joshua Shanker, BofA Securities: "let's talk about improved conversion. What does that mean actually in terms of operations?" President, CEO & Director Tooth: "the introduction of our coinsurance and deductible expansions" was "the first and perhaps most meaningful movement," and "we've talked about this previously with the investments in technology, the improvements in user experience, really helping to lean into value proposition commentary, AI, chatbots."

  • Joshua Shanker, BofA Securities: "is there a breakdown of gross new pets from the underwritten versus the MGA pets for the quarter?" Chief Financial Officer Qureshi: "No, that's not there. The majority is coming from core, however, in the quarter."

  • Joshua Shanker, BofA Securities: "Is there any indication on first year retention being better" and "what the drivers are"? President, CEO & Director Tooth: "First year, we would expect to be a little bit less so because we're adding pets at a higher clip," while "the introduction of the coinsurance and deductible appears early signs that we're having some benefits."

  • Joshua Shanker, BofA Securities: "$25 million is a nice even number" on buybacks; "How do you come to $25 million is the right number"? Chief Financial Officer Qureshi: "we want to have as much financial flexibility as possible" and "subsequent to the quarter end, we also paid down $15 million of debt in addition to the $25 million of share repurchase."

  • Wilma Jackson Burdis, Raymond James: "Subscription revenue grew mid-teens year-to-date. Do you think this is a good run rate?" Chief Financial Officer Qureshi: "The pricing increases... were also the lowest pricing increase we've seen going back to 2023" and "we've committed externally that we want to have mid-teens AOI growth over the 3 years."

  • Wilma Jackson Burdis, Raymond James: "plans to utilize the $18.5 million facility"? Chief Financial Officer Qureshi: "there's no pressing need to draw down on that, we have the capacity to be able to invest in the business."

  • Joshua Shanker, BofA Securities: "When will there be food available" and "what does a successful launch look like?" President, CEO & Director Tooth: "we anticipate being on track to actually start putting this out to market somewhere in the middle of next year" and "very limited contribution to revenue" over "the next 18 months" because "The successful launch for us is essentially making sure the logistics work."

  • Wilma Jackson Burdis, Raymond James: "pricing and pet cost inflation into 2027"? President, CEO & Director Tooth: "we expect to see what we have now considered consistently elevated costs of double-digit inflation" and "we are expecting to see continued double-digit inflation in 2027."

  • Brandon Vazquez, William Blair: "how the quality of the leads" and "identified pathways yet to use AI"? President, CEO & Director Tooth: "lead volume has actually been very solid" and "AI has been really interesting for us" because "We rank very well from an agentic search perspective."

  • Brandon Vazquez, William Blair: "maybe talk to us a little bit about the growth" for 2027? Chief Financial Officer Qureshi: "we'll provide guidance on the next call" and "you're starting to see a little bit more balance between pricing and pet count."

Sentiment Analysis

  • Analysts: slightly positive, with multiple questions pushing for operating detail and durability (e.g., "What does that mean actually in terms of operations?" and "what the drivers are"), alongside probing on capital allocation ("Why not just buy the stock at a cheap price").

  • Management: positive in prepared remarks and measured in Q&A, emphasizing execution and durability (e.g., "This is sustainable. It's what's really exciting for us is this isn't a one-off campaign." and "we'll provide guidance on the next call").

  • Versus last quarter: the current call reinforced acceleration themes with larger, more detailed discussion of conversion, buybacks executed, and explicit inflation expectations ("we are expecting to see continued double-digit inflation in 2027"), compared to Q2’s more normalization-oriented framing ("It has come down and we expect that, that will normalize over time."). (President, CEO & Director Tooth)

Quarter-over-Quarter Comparison

  • Q3 highlighted execution against previously stated initiatives, including broader rollout progress ("expanded deductible and coinsurance options now implemented entirely across Canada and roughly 90% of the U.S.") versus Q2’s rollout status ("we're around 50% of the way through that journey"). (President, CEO & Director Tooth)

  • Capital return shifted from authorization to deployment: Q2 announced "the authorization of a $100 million share repurchase program"; Q3 reported "we repurchased approximately 830,000 shares at a cost of approximately $25 million." (Chief Financial Officer Qureshi)

  • Pets Best transition moved from announcement to execution steps: Q2 said the company "agreed with Pets Best to conclude our relationship following the third quarter of 2028"; Q3 said the transition is "now underway" with the book "beginning to move to a new underwriting partner in the fourth quarter of 2026." (Chief Financial Officer Qureshi)

Risks and Concerns

  • "We expect to see... double-digit inflation coming through" and "We see nothing to expect that to be easing." (President, CEO & Director Tooth)

  • "Very limited contribution to revenue" expected from Landspath during the near-term rollout window as execution focuses on logistics and veterinary workflow. (President, CEO & Director Tooth)

  • "Our revenue projections are subject to conversion rate movements predominantly between the U.S. and Canadian currencies." (Chief Financial Officer Qureshi)

Final Takeaway

Management framed Q3 as a record profitability and cash-flow quarter paired with improved acquisition efficiency and continued retention gains, while also advancing multiple longer-dated initiatives (a new digital insurance offering targeted for next summer and Landspath trials ahead of a 2027 launch). The company also tied its capital allocation to both reinvestment and shareholder returns, citing $25 million of buybacks in the quarter and a $15 million post-quarter debt repayment, and maintained guidance ranges for Q4 and full-year 2026 while calling for continued double-digit veterinary inflation into 2027.

data.title: Under Armour maintains fiscal 2027 adjusted operating income outlook of $140M-$160M while cutting gross margin expansion view to 170-220 bps
data.description:
Earnings Call Insights: Under Armour (UAA) fiscal Q2 2027

Management view

  • "Our focus at Under Armour is to build a stronger brand through compelling products and more consistent execution" (CEO Kevin Plank), adding, "This quarter, we delivered against our revenue expectation and exceeded our adjusted operating income outlook" (CEO Plank).
  • "Our cleated business in American football... grew double digits in the quarter with higher average selling prices and market share gains" (CEO Plank), and "Under Armour is now the #2 brand in football cleats in the U.S." (CEO Plank).
  • "An early example of this work is our decision to transition our youth apparel business to an expanded licensing model with Centric Brands" (CEO Plank), and "Beginning in fall '27, the model should reduce inventory, working capital and operating complexity" (CEO Plank).
  • "We're simplifying our product line as well, targeting a reduction of nearly 50% in SKUs from the level when I returned in 2024" (CEO Plank), and "We've also removed more than 60% of materials while increasing global product commonality" (CEO Plank).
  • "Tech Helix... at $35... should be a multimillion unit program for us at full price" (CEO Plank). Separately, CEO Plank said "The Armour Short's patent-pending design launches in December at $80 for adults and $55 for kids on ua.com and in 500 DICK'S Sporting Goods stores in the U.S." (CEO Plank).
  • "Over the past several months, we've established a more unified marketing model" (CEO Plank) under "Chief Marketing Officer" Simon Pestridge (CEO Plank), and "we plan to introduce one major product story each month throughout the calendar year" (CEO Plank).
  • "Revenue declined 7% to $1.2 billion" (CFO Reza Taleghani) and "Gross margin was 47%, down 30 basis points" (CFO Taleghani).

Outlook

  • "We are maintaining the expectation that revenue will decline at a mid-single-digit rate" (CFO Taleghani), while noting, "current traffic and macroeconomic pressures could result in North America being down modestly more than the mid-single-digit decline we previously anticipated" (CFO Taleghani).
  • "For fiscal '27, gross margin, we now expect expansion of 170 to 220 basis points compared with our previous expectation of 220 to 270 basis points" (CFO Taleghani), adding, "The 50 basis point reduction in our gross margin outlook reflects ongoing elevated fuel and freight costs, planned markdowns to improve inventory alignment and a stronger U.S. dollar" (CFO Taleghani).
  • "We continue to expect full year adjusted operating income in the $140 million to $160 million range" (CFO Taleghani) and "full year adjusted diluted earnings per share of $0.08 to $0.12" (CFO Taleghani).
  • "Turning to our third quarter. We expect revenue to decline approximately 8% to 9%" (CFO Taleghani) and "we expect adjusted operating income to range from a loss of $5 million to a profit of $5 million with an adjusted diluted loss per share of $0.01 to $0.03" (CFO Taleghani).

Financial results

  • "Wholesale revenue decreased 6% to $725 million" (CFO Taleghani), "Direct-to-consumer revenue decreased 8% to $494 million" (CFO Taleghani), and "Licensing revenue decreased 4% to $28 million" (CFO Taleghani).
  • "Footwear revenue decreased 11% to $234 million" (CFO Taleghani), while "selected cleated businesses and run grew" (CFO Taleghani). "Accessories revenue decreased 7% to $105 million" (CFO Taleghani).
  • "SG&A decreased 4% to $557 million" (CFO Taleghani) and "Second quarter operating income was $15 million or $25 million adjusted" (CFO Taleghani).
  • "We ended the quarter with $1.1 billion in inventory, up 4% year-over-year" (CFO Taleghani), and "The approximate $200 million reduction in our revenue outlook in August left inventory above our planned sales needs" (CFO Taleghani).
  • "We ended the quarter with $285 million in cash and $190 million of borrowings under our $1.1 billion revolving credit facility" (CFO Taleghani).

  • Simeon Siegel, Guggenheim: asked how product excitement translates into pricing power, margin capture, and North America stabilization timing; CEO Plank responded, "the biggest place we've fallen down has just been in our confidence storytelling" and emphasized "product... marketing... distribution" while adding, "Marketing remains our largest opportunity as a brand to turn the trajectory of our business"; CFO Taleghani added, "we are looking at gross margin improvement over the course of the year".
  • Jay Sole, UBS: asked how UA measures brand momentum and what drove the gross margin guide change; CEO Plank said, "in Q2, we saw consideration rise over 19% year-over-year and brand perception up over 24%" and described "significantly reducing things like performance marketing"; CFO Taleghani said the "single biggest negative" behind the gross margin change was "logistics freight impacts".

Sentiment analysis

  • Analyst tone slightly negative, centered on promotional pressure, inventory risk, and the Q4 embedded assumptions, including requests to "unpack" the inflection and clarify the licensing economics.
  • Management tone slightly positive in prepared remarks with repeated emphasis on simplification and product-led storytelling, while responses acknowledged external pressure such as "a bit of a promotional marketplace" (CEO Plank) and "very promotional" conditions (CFO Taleghani).
  • Versus the prior quarter, guidance language showed tighter caution on gross margin expansion, while management continued to stress discipline and brand elevation; analysts remained focused on North America demand, promotions, and inventory cleanup.

Quarter-over-quarter comparison

  • In fiscal Q1, CEO Plank led with, "We're lowering our revenue outlook for the year while maintaining our adjusted operating income expectation" (CEO Plank); in fiscal Q2, he said, "we delivered against our revenue expectation and exceeded our adjusted operating income outlook" (CEO Plank).
  • In fiscal Q1, CFO Taleghani said, "we continue to expect expansion of approximately 220 to 270 basis points" in gross margin (CFO Taleghani); in fiscal Q2, he revised that to "expansion of 170 to 220 basis points" (CFO Taleghani).
  • In fiscal Q2, management introduced a new structural move not described in Q1 prepared remarks: "transition our youth apparel business to an expanded licensing model" (CEO Plank).

Risks and concerns

  • "Traffic remained the primary challenge, particularly in North America" (CFO Taleghani) and the company described "a highly competitive environment" that is "very promotional" in North America and the U.K. (CFO Taleghani).
  • "We ended the quarter with $1.1 billion in inventory, up 4% year-over-year" (CFO Taleghani), with mitigation described as "reducing future buys and taking targeted sell-through actions to release working capital and strengthen liquidity" (CFO Taleghani).
  • Supply chain disruptions were flagged, as CFO Taleghani said Middle East conflict headwinds are assumed at "about $45 million... up from the $35 million we cited previously" (CFO Taleghani).

Final takeaway

Management framed fiscal Q2 as a quarter where revenue fell but adjusted profitability ran ahead of its internal outlook, while reiterating a full-year revenue decline at a mid-single-digit rate and holding full-year adjusted operating income at $140 million to $160 million and adjusted EPS at $0.08 to $0.12. The call emphasized a sharper brand playbook built around SKU simplification, monthly product storytelling, and selective category proof points (including football cleats share gains), alongside a reduced gross margin expansion outlook tied to freight, FX, and planned inventory actions, plus a strategic shift to an expanded youth licensing model intended to reduce inventory and working capital beginning fall '27.
